claims.text: Severe lattice distortion governs intrinsic thermal stability and resistance to atomic diffusion in nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HENA.
Severe lattice distortion suppresses screw-dislocation mobility.
The proposed stability mechanism reduces the effective activation energy for vacancy migration.
High configurational entropy reduces the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation.
Random elemental distributions create local strain fields that pin or impede dislocations.
The local strain fields created by random elemental distributions impede atomic migration.
Below a critical nanoparticle size, surface energy dominates over bulk-like entropy and lattice-distortion effects.
A high surface-to-volume ratio lowers the energy barrier for phase separation or structural collapse.
Nanoparticles larger than approximately 20 nm will retain a single-phase structure up to 900 degrees Celsius.
Nanoparticles larger than approximately 20 nm will exhibit minimal diffusion and precipitation up to 900 degrees Celsius.
The proposed nanoparticles will remain elastically stable up to 900 degrees Celsius.
The proposed nanoparticles will exhibit intrinsic ductility at elevated temperatures.
Particles below the critical size will undergo rapid phase separation, amorphization, or surface reconstruction at temperatures substantially below the bulk melting point.
Traditional alloy stability is determined primarily by phase diagrams and thermodynamic-equilibrium calculations such as CALPHAD.
High-entropy alloys are assumed to be intrinsically stable against phase separation at every size scale solely because of configurational entropy.
The exact critical size for a transition from bulk-like to surface-dominated behavior is uncertain.
The cited mechanistic evidence primarily concerns bulk alloys rather than five-component high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Equilibrium CALPHAD oxidation predictions for CrMnFeCoNi can fail when kinetic limitations and experimental timescales are neglected.
Corrosion of Cr18Mn27Fe27.5Ni27.5 in molten FLiBe can follow conventional thermodynamic stability rules rather than unique high-entropy or sluggish-diffusion effects.
Magnetic ordering or composition-specific electronic effects could override lattice distortion as the dominant mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis associates resistance to diffusion with a reduced vacancy-migration activation energy, while the mechanism claims that atomic migration is impeded. Lowering a migration activation energy would ordinarily facilitate rather than suppress vacancy-mediated migration unless an additional compensating mechanism is specified.
